summary: CONF3 fan-out, REVIEWED FRESH on the rebased head. The fc377ea7 review and its verification were NOT carried forward; every claim below was re-derived against base fd3e31dd (SIL1 merged). RESOLUTION INTEGRITY, the specific risk of this rebase: #902 and #903 both edited the post-commit region of the v2 exit emitter, so I checked that neither eroded the other. All SIL1 symbols survive on this head — _V2_EXIT_MAX_REJECTS_PER_EPISODE = 20 (:464) and _V2_EXIT_REJECT_ALARM_THRESHOLD_SCHWAB = 8 (:471) unchanged, both counters, the threshold function, the publish path and the announced set all present — and the diff fd3e31dd..eb44cb35 DELETES ZERO SIL1 lines. SIL1's alarm still publishes AFTER session.commit() and outside the try, so an alert-write failure still cannot roll back the broker result; CONF3 layers its explicit emitter outcome returns around that block without moving it. CONF3 CLAIMS RE-DERIVED: fan-out via _v2_accounts() at :1082; the bound row resolved INSIDE the per-account loop at :1117 so each leg binds its own oms_managed_positions row; one decision still deduped on the Schwab source_fill_id at :1079 with no Webull evaluation row; release gated by _v2_exit_reject_total >= the 20 ceiling at :4269 and by RTH; ZERO new settings or flags in the entire diff (grepped for added self.settings.* and got nothing), so fan-out OFF stays byte-identical; both false 'LEFT IN PLACE' log lines removed and replaced with wording conditional on whether protection was actually released. STALL RISK CHECKED AND ABSENT: the inline await of _attach_webull_protection at :3992 sits inside a coroutine that _spawn_confirmation_webull_recovery (:4063) launches with asyncio.create_task (:4071) holding a strong reference with a done-callback, so the bounded 5-attempt retry never runs on the quote loop — this matters because the original _spawn_webull_protection docstring says the attach must never stall a fill. MY OWN MUTATIONS, not codex's: source-account-only fan-out -> 13 failed / 50 passed; binding every leg to the source account's row -> 10 failed / 53 passed; restored -> 63 passed. I also reproduced BOTH halves of codex's honest inert-mutation report: removing the fresh-flat interval finalizer at :4104 turns test_released_webull_pair_fresh_flat_preserves_interval_in_summary RED at exactly released_unprotected_seconds_max=0.000 instead of 4.000, while removing the RECOVERY-path finalizer at :3981 leaves the ENTIRE 17-test fan-out suite GREEN. CONTROLLED PAIR, full unfiltered tests/unit against this PR's own base: base fd3e31dd 46 failed / 3232 passed, head 46 failed / 3249 passed, delta +17, and the failure sets DIFFED BY NAME are IDENTICAL. Codex reported 55/3223 and 55/3240 — a different count but the SAME +17 delta and the same 3295 total, so the 9-test gap is environment-sensitive, the same discrepancy recorded on the #898 pin, and the identical-sets result holds independently in both environments. validate PASS on both runs. LIMITATION THIS PIN DOES NOT COVER, recorded rather than withheld because the shipped behaviour is correct and only its regression-proofing is partial: the recovery path's interval finalization (resolution=flat, :3981) has NO controlling test — it is inert to mutation. In production, skipping it would leave the symbol in _confirmation_unprotected_since forever, inflating released_unprotected_current and the max duration, which is precisely the 'count of positions currently in that state' the operator asked for. A control for that branch should be added; it is a test addition, not a behaviour change. ALSO NOT COVERED: the live close itself remains UNEXERCISED — post-#897 the confirmation exit has never fired in production, and no test can supply that.
